title: Admin - Assign Permissions to Limited Access Admin - Functional Test Plan
overview: Functional testing of the Admin User & Role Management - Assign Permissions to Limited Access Admin feature on the Y4J platform. This feature allows Super Admins to assign specific module permissions to Limited-Access Admins via checkboxes. The permissions list includes User Management, Vendor Management, Product Approval, Content Management, Content Moderation, Comment Management, Analytics, and System Settings. At least one permission must be selected, and selected permissions are saved with the admin record and displayed on the admin card. Covers happy path, validation, edge cases, and error handling.

testCases.title: Permissions section displays all available permissions as checkboxes
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Add Internal Admin modal is open with 'Limited-Access Admin' role selected.
steps: Open the Add Internal Admin modal
Observe the permissions section that appears
expectedResults: A permissions section is displayed with checkboxes
The following permissions are listed: User Management, Vendor Management, Product Approval, Content Management, Content Moderation, Comment Management, Analytics, System Settings
All 8 permissions are visible as selectable checkboxes
No permissions are pre-selected by default (or a default set is pre-selected)
testCases.postconditions: All 8 permission checkboxes are visible and selectable

testCases.title: Permissions are selectable via checkboxes - single selection
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Permissions section is visible with all checkboxes unchecked.
steps: In the permissions section, click on the 'Dashboard' checkbox
expectedResults: The 'Dashboard' checkbox becomes checked (shows checkmark or filled state)
Only the clicked checkbox is selected — others remain unchecked
The checkbox is toggleable (can be unchecked by clicking again)

testCases.title: Multiple permissions can be selected simultaneously
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Permissions section is visible.
expectedResults: All three checkboxes are checked simultaneously
Multiple selections are allowed
Each checkbox operates independently
Selecting one does not deselect others

testCases.title: At least one permission must be selected - validation error
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Add Internal Admin modal is open with all fields filled except permissions (none selected).
steps: Fill in Name, Email, and select 'Limited-Access Admin' role
Do NOT select any permission checkboxes
expectedResults: The form does NOT submit
A validation error is displayed (e.g., 'At least one permission must be selected')
The modal remains open for the user to select permissions
The 'Add Admin' button may be disabled until a permission is selected
testCases.postconditions: Form submission is blocked without at least one permission

testCases.title: Selected permissions are saved with admin record
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Add Internal Admin modal is open.
steps: Fill in valid Name and Email
Find the newly created admin card
expectedResults: The admin is created successfully
After page refresh, the admin card still shows the same 3 permissions
Permissions are persisted to the backend (not just in-memory)
The saved permissions match exactly what was selected
testCases.postconditions: Permissions are persisted and survive page refresh

testCases.title: Permissions appear in admin card after creation
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. A new Limited-Access Admin has just been created with specific permissions.
steps: Create a new Limited-Access Admin with permissions: 'Comment Moderation', 'Product Management'
After modal closes, observe the new admin card in the list
expectedResults: The new admin card displays a 'Permissions:' section
The permissions section shows tags/badges for 'Comment Moderation' and 'Product Management'
Only the selected permissions are shown (not all 8)
The permissions are displayed immediately without page refresh
testCases.postconditions: Selected permissions are visible on the admin card

testCases.title: Deselecting a permission removes it from selection
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Permissions section is visible with some checkboxes checked.
steps: Click on 'Vendor Management' checkbox again to deselect it
expectedResults: 'Vendor Management' checkbox becomes unchecked
'User Management' and 'Analytics' remain checked
The deselection is immediate and visual
Only 2 permissions remain selected

testCases.title: Selecting all permissions equals Super Admin behavior
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Add Internal Admin modal is open with 'Limited-Access Admin' role.
expectedResults: The admin is created successfully with all 8 permissions
The admin card shows all permissions listed
The admin effectively has the same access as a Super Admin
The role still shows 'Limited Access Admin' (role label doesn't auto-change)
OR the system may show a warning/info message that all permissions selected equals Super Admin access
testCases.postconditions: Admin with all permissions is created (functionally equivalent to Super Admin)

testCases.title: Permission list fails to load - error handling
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. API for permissions list is configured to fail.
steps: Open the Add Internal Admin modal
Observe the permissions section when the API fails to load the list
expectedResults: An error message is displayed (e.g., 'Failed to load permissions. Please try again.')
The form cannot be submitted without permissions loaded
A retry option may be available
The modal does not crash or show a blank permissions area
testCases.postconditions: Permission load failure is handled gracefully

testCases.title: Permissions section only appears for Limited-Access Admin role
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Add Internal Admin modal is open.
steps: Open the Add Internal Admin modal
expectedResults: With 'Super Admin' role: permissions section is either hidden or shows all permissions as pre-selected/locked
With 'Limited-Access Admin' role: permissions section appears with selectable checkboxes
The permissions section is contextual to the selected role

testCases.title: Permission checkboxes are independent - no cascading selection
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Permissions section is visible.
steps: Observe if any other checkboxes are automatically selected
Observe if any other checkboxes change state
expectedResults: Selecting one permission does NOT auto-select any other permission
Each checkbox is fully independent
No cascading or dependent selections occur
User has full control over which permissions to assign

testCases.title: Permissions are correctly mapped to module access
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. A Limited-Access Admin has been created with only 'Partner Management' and 'Product Management' permissions.
steps: Create a Limited-Access Admin with only 'Partner Management' and 'Product Management'
Log out and log in as the newly created Limited-Access Admin
expectedResults: The Limited-Access Admin can only access Partner Management and Product Management modules
Other modules (User Management, Content Management, etc.) are not accessible
Navigation only shows the permitted modules
Attempting to access restricted modules shows an access denied message

testCases.title: Select all / Deselect all functionality (if available)
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Permissions section is visible.
steps: Look for a 'Select All' or 'Deselect All' option in the permissions section
expectedResults: If 'Select All' exists: all 8 checkboxes become checked
If 'Deselect All' exists: all checkboxes become unchecked
If neither exists: this test is N/A (manual selection only)
Bulk selection/deselection works correctly

testCases.title: Permission labels match the actual module names in the system
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin. Permissions section is visible.
steps: Compare with the actual module names in the admin sidebar navigation
expectedResults: Permission labels match or closely correspond to the sidebar navigation module names
Users can clearly understand which module each permission grants access to
No ambiguous or unclear permission names exist
testCases.postconditions: Permission labels are clear and match system modules
